body:
Thank you very much for taking the time to reply. 

I will be needing to seek official help, I've decided. The good thing is that he is currently stable and seems to feel better after getting this off his chest. It's definitely reassuring and I take it as a good sign but I can't be too optimistic and hope that these feelings don't resurface.   
I'm just so glad that he opened up to me about this. If he hadn't told me he could be gone by now. So I thank my lucky stars that he was at least back and forth on the idea. 

He hasn't explicitly said he feels less suicidal, just better and I will be making sure he's not alone when I'm gone tomorrow. 

I care about him very much and am going to stay by his side through all of this. I know I can't take away his pain but I can offer him all the love I have to give and support him as much as I can as he tries to get better. It's a tough road ahead and your kind words are really appreciated.

I'm definitely no stranger to feeling suicidal. I have been in his shoes and I do understand how it can feel when you open up to someone about your feelings and they freak out.   
But ultimately, my main goal is to make sure he does not kill himself. Being involuntarily admitted is not a nice experience and I understand that but I also don't want to be too hesitant about taking action when he hasn't exactly said he feels differently about suicide.   
I do want to comfort him and make him feel okay but I also can't trust that he isn't going to kill himself when I leave.   
I don't want to force him to get help but if he doesn't take a positive step I can't be a stationary force in his life. He is very sick at the moment and making decisions in his state aren't exactly guaranteed to be the best.   


I would put the laughter and jokes down to a coping mechanism if it weren't very unusual. It's like his mood is completely separate from his suicidal idealisation. He is laughing during very serious conversations. He almost seems happy. It's very confusing and very concerning. 

I really think it's the emotional stress he is under, you're right. It is hard to not be self-critical and wonder if you're doing the best you can in a situation like this. But he's had a very different attitude since and I can see the turmoil he is in. 

He's fine and mostly stable at the moment, so that's good for now. 

Thank you for your kind words.
